title: Rosalind and the Veil
premise: Juniper Ravensworth carves bones into instruments of memory and keeps the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things, a trade in relics, oaths, and borrowed time. When a mute child arrives speaking Vellish — the tongue of a country erased from every map and ledger forty years ago — Juniper discovers her own bone-carving gift is inherited from that vanished land, and that the Veil which swallowed it is now hunting its last speakers. Guided by the child's fragmented memories and the dead who remember what the living were made to forget, Juniper must find the Door Out: the single threshold through which the old country can be either restored or finally laid to rest. In the end she learns survival itself was the price paid — her grandmother bought the family's escape by selling the country's name — and Juniper must choose between reclaiming Velland at the cost of everyone born since, or carrying its memory forward as its final living ledger.
about_author: Ulyana Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the belongings of families displaced by border redraws. She writes fantasy about what survives when countries don't, and lives near a coastline that has changed hands four times.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She balances the guild's accounts, carving a dead woman's name into a rib-bone so her daughter can hear one last goodbye. Establishes her gift, her debts, and her careful distance from other people. Emotional beat: competent loneliness.

chapters.title: A Knock at Odd Hours
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A child appears at the guild door at night, barefoot, unafraid, speaking a language no living person should know. The guild's senior partners refuse her; Juniper, hearing the child's words as grief rather than nonsense, takes her in. Beat: reluctant compassion.

chapters.title: What the Bones Say
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Testing the child with carved bone, Juniper hears not the child's voice but hundreds layered beneath it — the dead of an unnamed place. She names the girl Wren. First hint that Juniper's own inheritance is implicated. Beat: unease becoming wonder.

chapters.title: The Guild of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, fragmentary and strange. Through the child's eyes the guildhall is full of doors that hum, and one door at the back that aches. Introduces Master Corvane, who wants Wren appraised as inventory. Beat: wonder shadowed by threat.

chapters.title: Vellish
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. An antiquarian confirms the language: Velland, a country struck from maps after the Reckoning, its survivors sworn to silence. Juniper realizes she half-understands words she was never taught. Beat: the past reaching into the present.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Box
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Searching her late grandmother's effects, Juniper finds a bone stylus and a page torn from a ledger written in Vellish — with her grandmother's handwriting. The word 'price' recurs. Beat: betrayal germinating.

chapters.title: Corvane Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Master Corvane's POV. He offers to buy Wren outright, claiming the guild has standing orders for 'last speakers.' His internal logic is chillingly reasonable. Beat: the machinery of commerce closing around a child.

chapters.title: The Dead Who Wait
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. At the bone-yard, the dead press close for the first time in years, repeating a phrase in Vellish: 'the Door Out stands where the name stood.' Juniper understands they want something done before the Veil finishes its work. Beat: dread with purpose.

chapters.title: Running the Ledger Backward
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Following entries in her grandmother's hand, Juniper traces a payment received the year Velland fell — enormous, anonymous, denominated in memory rather than coin. Beat: the ground tilting under everything she believed.

chapters.title: Wren Remembers Fire
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A nightmare floods Juniper's shared room with remembered smoke; Wren relives the night the Veil took her city. Juniper holds her and, touching her carved beads, sees fragments herself. Beat: intimacy forged in horror.

chapters.title: The Sworn Silence
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She finds three surviving Velland-born elders in the capital's tenements. Two refuse to speak; one, Maren, tells her the survivors swore an oath enforced by the Veil itself — break it and be unmade. Beat: the cost of truth made explicit.

chapters.title: Inventory
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. He files papers declaring Wren guild property, citing precedent from the Reckoning era when Vellish refugees were traded as 'resonant goods.' Beat: institutional evil, calm and procedural.

chapters.title: Theft of a Small Person
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper steals Wren out of the guildhall through the humming doors, using her ledger knowledge to forge their own exit entry. They flee the city. Beat: decisive rebellion, exhilaration laced with terror.

chapters.title: Road Made of Forgetting
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. On the road toward old Velland's borders, villages they pass have no records of the country next door; innkeepers deny it ever existed. The Veil erases as they travel. Beat: isolation deepening.

chapters.title: Maren's Map
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The old woman decides the oath matters less than the child, and gives Juniper a map stitched from memory — the only map of Velland left anywhere. Warns: the Door Out opens once a generation, soon. Beat: fragile hope.

chapters.title: Hunters of the Veil
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Grey figures begin following them — the Veil's wardens, faceless, who unmake spoken memories. Wren's presence draws them like blood draws sharks. Beat: pursuit begins.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Fee
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. To cross the river that marked Velland's edge, the ferryman demands a memory as toll. Juniper pays with her mother's face, and grieves it immediately. Beat: first personal installment of the theme's price.

chapters.title: Country Without a Name
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. They cross into terrain that is Velland and isn't — fields that answer to old names, ruins that rebuild when Wren speaks. The dead here are thick as fog. Beat: awe and homesickness for a home never known.

chapters.title: The Choir of the Unburied
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. In a sunken cathedral, the Vellish dead gather to Juniper's carving, begging to be recorded. She spends nights inscribing names until her hands bleed. Beat: vocation transformed into burden.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Bought
chapters.summary: Interleaved POV, the dead speaking through bone. Juniper learns the truth: her grandmother sold Velland's true name to the Veil's makers in exchange for her family's passage out — the founding payment behind the Ravensworth fortune. Beat: devastating revelation.

chapters.title: Anger, Carved
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper rages at her grandmother's ghost, at the inheritance built on erasure, nearly destroys her tools. Wren quietly returns the stylus to her hand. Beat: rage transmuting into resolve.

chapters.title: Corvane Closes In
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. He has tracked them with guild writs and hired wardens, intending to deliver Wren to the Veil's brokers himself — there is profit in finishing an erasure. Beat: net tightening.

chapters.title: The Village That Chose to Forget
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A survivor settlement where people voluntarily surrendered their Vellish memories to live safely. One man begs Juniper to carve his forgotten daughter's name back into him. Beat: mercy versus safety.

chapters.title: Wren Speaks Plainly
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reveals she isn't random: she is the last child born inside the Veil, sent out through a crack as the Door began sealing. She remembers where the Door stands — under the erased capital. Beat: the quest gains its destination.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Milestone
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Wardens attack; Maren, arriving to help, breaks her oath aloud to drive them off and is unmade mid-sentence, dissolving into forgetting. Her sacrifice buys their escape. Beat: grief and gratitude entwined.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival, Itemized
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper audits her grandmother's full ledger and finds the terms: if Velland's name is restored, all descendants of the bargain forfeit their claim on existence. Saving a country may unmake her line. Beat: the central dilemma crystallized.

chapters.title: Corvane's Confession
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Cornered by Juniper, Corvane admits he is Vellish-born too, and chose the winning side long ago; his cruelty is self-loathing wearing a merchant's coat. Beat: antagonist humanized without absolution.

chapters.title: March on the Erased Capital
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. With the dead as escort and Wren as compass, they walk into the heart of the Veil, where streets exist only when named aloud. Beat: grim pilgrimage, courage sustained by company.

chapters.title: The Door Out
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Beneath the ruined palace they find it: a threshold of white bone, sealed with a lock shaped like a mouth, waiting for Velland's true name. Beat: arrival, breath held.

chapters.title: The Lock and the Key
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Only a speaker born inside the Veil can pronounce the name through the lock — but speaking it will spend Wren entirely, body and memory. Beat: the cost lands on the smallest shoulders.

chapters.title: Juniper Refuses
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper refuses to let Wren pay, proposing instead to leave the Door shut and carry Velland in ledgers and bone forever. The dead protest; Wren defies her. Beat: love arguing with duty.

chapters.title: Corvane's Choice
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Arriving with wardens, Corvane instead turns on them — he unlocks the guild's stolen Vellish archive and adds its names to Juniper's, choosing memory over profit at last. Beat: redemption purchased late.

chapters.title: The Veil Speaks
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The Veil manifests as her grandmother's voice, offering Juniper the same bargain her ancestor took: walk away rich and alive, and the erasure completes cleanly. Beat: temptation at maximum pressure.

chapters.title: The Answer Is No
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper counters with her own ledger-entry: she assumes the debt, all of it, and offers her inherited claim on existence as collateral so Wren needn't be spent. Beat: self-sacrifice as bookkeeping — the novel's thesis made action.

chapters.title: Speaking Velland
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren speaks the true name through the bone lock, but instead of dying she pours the name into Juniper's carved bones — distributed across thousands of small memorials, too many pieces for any Veil to swallow. Beat: climax; cleverness and courage fused.

chapters.title: Unmaking the Veil
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The Veil tears as names return to fields, ruins, rivers. The dead of Velland pass through the Door Out at last — not back to life, but onward, at rest. Juniper pays her collateral: her gift of hearing fades. Beat: catharsis and loss together.

chapters.title: After the Doors Close
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Velland exists again on maps; its people return to rebuilt towns. Juniper, deaf now to the dead, keeps only ordinary silence — and finds it bearable because it was chosen. Beat: quiet aftermath.

chapters.title: The New Ledger
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper reopens the guild under new rules: nothing impossible is traded, only remembered. Wren, adopted, becomes her apprentice in plain carving. Corvane, diminished, donates the archive. Beat: restoration with scars.

chapters.title: What Wren Carries
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren teaches Vellish to other children in the returned capital; Juniper visits and cannot understand the language anymore, and weeps gladly. Beat: inheritance passed forward, transformed.

chapters.title: Rosalind and the Veil
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Among her grandmother's papers Juniper finally finds the origin: Rosalind Ravensworth, the ancestor whose choice began everything, and a letter asking forgiveness. Juniper writes the closing ledger line — debt assumed, debt discharged, story kept. Beat: reconciliation across generations; the tale seals shut.
